facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s without a prior history of arrhythmia
cough and shortness of breath during the COVID-19 pandemic
Cardiac auscultation: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops
Pulmonary auscultation: Inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs
Regular, narrow complex tachycardia with rate of 170 beats/min

concepts.why: The patient has a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR test, cough, shortness of breath, and inspiratory crackles in bilateral lung bases, which are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
The patient developed palpitations and had a regular, narrow complex tachycardia with a rate of 170 beats/min on ECG, which is consistent with atrial tachycardia.

aliases: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
concepts.why: The patient has mild diastolic dysfunction on echocardiogram and inspiratory crackles in bilateral lung bases, which may indicate heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

rationales.F02: Cough and shortness of breath are common symptoms of COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F06: Increased respiratory rate can be seen in COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F10: Inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F11: Positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR test is diagnostic of COVID-19.
rationales.F12: Regular, narrow complex tachycardia is consistent with atrial tachycardia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with cough, shortness of breath, and a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR test, which strongly supports COVID-19 pneumonia, and the subsequent development of palpitations can be explained by the stress of the pneumonia on the body, including the heart.
